svg.title: Annex A4 · Download in GitHub Actions and per-source fallbacks
svg.desc: Each source's fallback ladder in the daily run: official URL, Peru, n8n and console copies, mirrors, Internet Archive and previous publication, with their time limits and provenance.
svg.text: Annex A4 · Download in GitHub Actions and per-source fallbacks

How the daily update gets each value: it follows the registry, requests the official URL from GitHub servers in the US and, if it does not answer, walks down a ladder of fallbacks to the last good value already published. Every answer
keeps its channel, URL, date and sha256.
Details these boxes of the full diagram: Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher), Internet Archive (Wayback), Previous publication (live data/), Actions cache: reader feeds.
data-* branches · Internet Archive · live site
value, channel and provenance of each source

g.title: 1. Channel plan → 1 · Official URL: the URL's plan. If the URL belongs to Actions it is requested; if not, the copy first; if forbidden, it is not requested.
2. Reader-feed state → 1 · Official URL: reader feeds: every 20 h or more. A single try with no retry on 429 or 5xx; between reads the last state stays.
3. Time limits → 1 · Official URL: run time limit. After the limit, each source goes on with its copies or its previous value, so the run gets to publish.
4. 1 · Official URL → 2 · A collector's copy: no answer. The copy is used if the request fails or answers something empty or of another type.
5. 2 · A collector's copy → 3 · Official mirror: no copy. It moves on to the source's next official mirror.
6. 3 · Official mirror → 4 · Internet Archive: mirrors fail. With every URL exhausted, it looks for each one's archived copy.
7. 4 · Internet Archive → 5 · Last published value: no archived copy. If the archive has no copy either, the last good value is kept.
8. data-peru → 2 · A collector's copy: Peru copy. Up to 7 days; warning at 36 h and relay-goal-missed if the communiqué or report PDF is missing.
9. data-n8n → 2 · A collector's copy: n8n copy. Up to 72 h; warning at 36 h.
10. data-manual → 2 · A collector's copy: uploaded PDF. Looked up with the document's own URL (or manual://enfen-informe/<id>).
11. web.archive.org → 4 · Internet Archive: CDX and id_. After the official sources' 8 minutes it is no longer queried.
12. Live site (data/) → 5 · Last published value: sources/<id>.json. The previous value is read from the published site; up to 3 tries for the history and the feed status.
13. 1 · Official URL → Reader and validation: the first valid answer. Any rung that answers (direct, copy, mirror or archive) goes to the reader.
14. 5 · Last published value → Value with provenance: carried value. Marked carried, with the date it was really obtained.
15. Reader and validation → Value with provenance: parsed value. The value, its format fingerprint and its plausibility warnings.
16. Value with provenance → Incidents: channel and attempts. Each use of a fallback leaves its incident with the attempts' detail.

Channel plan. registry/sources.json says who requests each URL: one not assigned to Actions is read from the copies first (with no copy, a single direct try); one forbidden by robots.txt is not requested. Technology: registry.url_channels.

g.title: Reader-feed state. reader-state.json in the Actions cache: when each reader feed was last requested and its notes not yet published. Restored at the start and saved at the end even if the run fails; main only. at least 20 h between requests. Technology: actions/cache.

g.title: Time limits. Official sources: 8 min in total and 5 min per request; ENFEN, ICEN and the ENSO discussion first. News: 60 s per feed. After the limit nothing more is requested.

g.title: 1 · Official URL. Up to 3 tries with growing waits on transient errors (DNS, 5xx, 429, timeout); 0.8 s between requests to the same server. After 3 failures in a row a server gets 1 try; after 5, it is skipped. direct channel. Technology: httpx, TLS + intermedios.
g.text: Up to 3 tries with growing waits on transient
between requests to the same server. After 3
failures in a row a server gets 1 try; after 5, it

g.title: 2 · A collector's copy. The copy of that same URL from Peru (up to 7 days), n8n (72 h) or the console (120 days), with status 200 and a verified sha256. If there are several, the newest wins. relay-peru, relay-n8n and relay-manual channels.
g.text: The copy of that same URL from Peru (up to 7
days), n8n (72 h) or the console (120 days),
with status 200 and a verified sha256. If there

g.title: 3 · Official mirror. The same with each declared mirror, in order (for example, the ENFEN mirror at the DHN), and its copy. mirror channel.
g.text: The same with each declared mirror, in order
(for example, the ENFEN mirror at the DHN),

g.title: 4 · Internet Archive. The newest copy with status 200, unchanged. For ENFEN, if it is older than a day, it asks for a new one (Save Page Now). News never uses it. archive and archive-fresh channels.

g.title: web.archive.org. CDX to search, id_ to fetch the original and /save/ for a new copy (only with ENSO_ARCHIVE_SAVE=1, on every run except a manual one that unticks it). Technology: CDX API, Save Page Now.

If something fails: what happens and which fallback takes over
The ENFEN portal does not answer from the US
The registry gives it to Peru: the data-peru copy is used and only without a
copy is it tried once; then the DHN mirror and the Internet Archive.
A copy branch does not exist or cannot be fetched
The folder goes empty and the run continues with the other fallbacks;
A server answers very slowly or not at all
Each request has a total time; after 3 failures the server gets a single try
and after 5 it is skipped for the run.
Nothing more is requested: each source goes on with its copies or its
previous value, and the run publishes.
It is published with its real date and the site shows “Current value not
A critical source has no value and no previous one
The run ends critical and nothing is deployed: yesterday's site stays.
